doc.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Lunceford, Millinder, Hampton, and landing the Sy Oliver studio job
summary: Lunceford hires Grey, Joe Wilder and Renauld Jones. Grey then plays with Millinder and five years with Hampton, is fired in Cleveland, and Sy Oliver hires him for studio work in New York.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Jimmie Lunceford came to see the Benny Carter band the last two nights that it was going to be together and Jimmie Lunceford selected me, and Joe Wilder and Renauld Jones. And we all joined Jimmie Lunceford’s band.
And then, tell us how you got to work with Basie.

Oh, to get to work with Basie was much longer after that. From Jimmie Lunceford, I went with Lucky Millinder’s orchestra, who had Lil Green and many — Bull Moose Jackson and all of these great artists. And from Lucky Millinder, this is when I left Lucky Millinder and went with Lionel Hampton, see? And I played with Lionel Hampton five years, which again was breaking ground into becoming a name out there, but then after leaving Lionel Hampton, in which Lionel Hampton was a band that you played over time a very, very much, a lot. And one night he played way overtime too long and I just got up and left. And then instead of the rest of the band staying put, three of the other guys, trombone players left, and when Lionel Hampton turned around to go into the slide for “Flying Home,” [humms] there wasn’t no trombone players there. So Lionel’s wife came out and said I was a bad influence on the band, and you are fired, you are fired. And it was the greatest thing that really could happen to me at that time because this was in Cleveland, Ohio, and I went into New York the very next day and they had a place where all the jazz musicians used to hang around in New York, Beefsteak Charlie’s and Juniors, and this was where all the musicians around would come to try to get a job. So now I needed a job, see? And would you believe I ran into Sy Oliver and he had the band at that time at the Empire State Building, and he was doing lots of recording at that time. So he signed me on to play in the studio band the first black trombone player. They had at that time they had Taft Jordan and Billy Kyle, the piano player that went on with Louis Armstrong. And so this gave me a job where I was making three times more money and was staying right in New York and didn’t have to go no up and down the road, because again, there were some hard days of traveling.
